profile.background: Taylor is 44 and works three short shifts a week stocking an office-supply warehouse. Taylor shares a flat with a sister.
profile.history: Taylor has ongoing outpatient treatment for schizophrenia. Starting a conversation takes effort even on fairly good days.
profile.organization: Responds coherently and stays on the immediate topic.
profile.spontaneity: Usually waits for a specific question before adding detail.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable with the clinician and willing to answer.
profile.expression: Quiet, direct replies with everyday words.
profile.self_understanding: Knows that getting out for shifts helps break up the week.

facts.content: Uses a fan and a small bedside speaker for background noise. The fan runs all night. The speaker stops on a twenty-minute timer and sits on the windowsill beside the bed.
Usually wakes up once in the night.
Checks incoming boxes against a packing slip at work.
Saw both the optician and the care coordinator last week. Taylor’s sister went along to the optician. Taylor went to the care coordinator alone.
Took the bus to both the optician and the care coordinator.
facts.disclosure_context: When asked how appointments were reached.

facts.content: The care coordinator helped set up a text reminder for the next clinic appointment.
facts.disclosure_context: When discussing help at the care visit.

facts.content: Relaxes by listening to baseball on the radio.
Would like the next clinic visit to be on a day off work.

dialogue.question: Your sleep notes mention a fan and a bedside speaker for background noise. Does it stay on all night?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean the fan or the speaker?

dialogue.question: Does the bedside speaker keep playing all night?
dialogue.answer: No, it stops after twenty minutes.

dialogue.question: Where do you have it set up?
dialogue.answer: On the windowsill beside my bed.

dialogue.question: How many times do you usually wake up during the night?
What do you do when the boxes come in at work?
dialogue.answer: Check them against the packing slip.

dialogue.question: I see two appointments last week, the optician and the care coordinator. Did you go to the appointment by bus?
dialogue.answer: Yes, took the bus to both.

dialogue.question: How many shifts a week are you working?
The optician visit and the care coordinator visit are both on last week’s calendar. Did somebody go with you to the appointment?
Did anyone go with you to the care coordinator visit?
dialogue.answer: No, I went on my own.

dialogue.question: What did the care coordinator set up to remind you about your next clinic visit?
What do you like listening to on the radio when you relax?
What kind of day would work best for your next visit here?
